title: Perturbation-scale ratios do not demonstrate improved cross-cohort Parkinson voice discrimination
abstract: We tested whether RAP/local-jitter and APQ3/local-shimmer ratios add discrimination beyond conventional perturbation, pitch and harmonicity measures. A fixed discovery-only ridge logistic model trained on 32 parsed Oxford subject identifiers was applied without target fitting to 40 independently collected Istanbul participants. Oxford subject-held-out AUC decreased from 0.7656 to 0.7500. Istanbul AUC increased from 0.6200 to 0.6375 (difference 0.0175; paired participant bootstrap 95% interval -0.0575 to 0.1050), while Brier score and log loss worsened. Training-and-target bootstrap and model/aggregation sensitivities did not demonstrate a reliable incremental benefit. The Oxford file contains 32 identifiers despite documentation describing 31 participants; this discrepancy, small cohorts, unmeasured confounding and different extraction pipelines limit inference. No clinical utility or novel physiological mechanism is established.
